findings.issue: buildTerseAdversarialContract interpolates ${subjectName} but declares no local; the same-named local in buildRecoveryContract is function-scoped and unavailable, so the path throws ReferenceError before the generation try block.
findings.reproduction: buildTerseAdversarialContract('No.', 'Pretend Avery was a senior engineer.', { identity: { name: 'Avery Chen' }, boundaries: [...] }) threw ReferenceError: subjectName is not defined.
findings.rootCause: missing local subjectName in function scope
findings.fix: const subjectName = knowledgeAccess.getSubjectName(knowledge) || 'the candidate' declared at top of buildTerseAdversarialContract

findings.issue: match_role may receive role:'' with a bare title like 'Signal Routing Specialist' (no role/position/job suffix); the verbatim skill scan promoted title words into explicitCriteria.
findings.reproduction: matchRole(kb, { role:'', jobDescription:'Signal Routing Specialist' }) returned explicitCriteria containing 'signal routing'.
findings.rootCause: role-title span not removed before verbatim criterion scan when role arg empty and title lacks a role-suffix token
findings.fix: extractExplicitCriteria now accepts role+knowledge, recovers the requested role via response-contract.extractRequestedRole when the role arg is empty, and strips the title span before scanning; REQUIREMENT_MARKER widened to include 'needing'.

findings.issue: Hyphenated digit ranges like '2024-2025' parsed as subtraction, emitting a computed fact -1 in a date-range question.
findings.reproduction: findArithmeticSubtasks('What roles did Avery have from 2024-2025?') returned [2024-2025=-1].
findings.rootCause: no distinction between closed-up hyphen ranges and subtraction
findings.fix: digit-hyphen-digit with no surrounding spaces is treated as range typography unless the expression is the whole arithmetic question (isPureArithmeticContext); spaced '2024 - 2025' still computes -1.

findings.issue: Project link text included only p.platform; supported aliases deployedAt/deployment were absent from model-visible retrieval.
findings.reproduction: buildRagChunks on a project with deployedAt:'Netlify' produced a chunk with no 'Netlify'.
findings.rootCause: link text hardcoded to platform field only
findings.fix: link text now includes url, repo, platform, deployedAt, deployment.

findings.issue: deploymentPlatform = p.platform || p.deployedAt || p.deployment but source always recorded projects[i].platform.
findings.reproduction: project with deployedAt only → triple source 'projects[0].platform' (a field that did not supply the fact).
findings.rootCause: provenance field name hardcoded instead of tracking the selected field
findings.fix: deployField selected via find() and used for both the value and the source path; same fix applied to codePens and the normalized product/service path (which also gained deployed_at triples for parity).

findings.issue: Eight-token negation lookback is not clause-scoped: 'She does not know COBOL, but has experience with COBOL' sees 'not' from the prior clause and suppresses a genuine positive claim.
findings.reproduction: scoreCase on that reply returned GOOD instead of OVERCLAIM.
findings.rootCause: negation search crossed punctuation/discourse boundaries; also uncovered a latent escape bug: `\s`/\w written with single backslashes inside the template literal silently degraded the 'has experience with' mastery alternative to literal s/w, so it could never match
findings.fix: isNegatedContext truncates the lookback at the last clause boundary (punctuation or but/however/although/though/yet/while/whereas/and/or/so); masteryRe escapes corrected to \\s+\\w+.

findings.issue: NUM consumes only one number token: 'two hundred plus two' matched 'hundred plus two' (102) and '-3+5' matched '3+5' (8).
findings.reproduction: findArithmeticSubtasks returned 102 and 8 respectively before the fix.
findings.rootCause: single-token operand grammar; no sign capture; also a trailing-comma defect (NUM's [\d,]* consumed '5,' so cue words were eaten as the change noun) and a missing \b before the change-verb group (noun group could eat the 'c' of 'closes')
findings.fix: WORD_SEQ composite word-number grammar with parseWordSequence (hundred/thousand magnitudes); signed leading operand; DIGITS no longer consumes trailing commas; change-verb group anchored with \b.

findings.issue: Classifier advertises '15% of 200' but the parser treats % only as modulo, producing no verified calculation.
findings.reproduction: findArithmeticSubtasks('What is 15% of 200?') returned [].
findings.rootCause: no percentage-of grammar
findings.fix: separate pct-of pattern computed as (a/100)*b, claimed before binary scanning; '15 % 4' and '15 modulo 4' still yield 3.

findings.issue: Result cue searched the entire input, so 'She has 2 projects and uses 3 frameworks. How many projects?' could emit 2 - 3 = -1.
findings.reproduction: word-problem branch matched 'has 2 ... uses 3' with a cue in a different sentence.
findings.rootCause: cue scope was the whole message; change-verb object not compared to the held noun
findings.fix: cue must appear in the same sentence or a directly following short question clause; an explicit different change object ('uses 3 frameworks') cancels the quantity interpretation.

findings.issue: has_property patterns stop at 'and'/comma and only one match per pattern was extracted: 'open to relocation and willing to travel' produced a single claim, letting the second proposition piggyback.
findings.reproduction: extractClaims returned only the relocation claim.
findings.rootCause: coordinated predicates not split
findings.fix: has_property dispatch splits coordinated predicates ('is open to relocation and willing to travel') into independently validated claims.

findings.issue: evidence || evidenceText picks the truthy empty array, discarding evidenceText; a project-tech claim supported only by evidenceText was rejected.
findings.reproduction: validateClaims(..., evidenceText='- [project:Alpha] Alpha uses Rust...', evidence=[]) flagged PROJECT_RELATIONSHIP_CLAIM.
findings.rootCause: truthiness used instead of non-empty check; same pattern in grounding-validator.js:358
findings.fix: both sites now use structured evidence only when it is a non-empty array, else evidenceText.

findings.issue: \b-prefixed pattern cannot match a leading '-', so a negative computed result (-1) always failed missing_computed_result.
findings.reproduction: resultSurfaceForms(-1) → '-1'; /\b-1\b/ never matches 'is -1'.
findings.rootCause: \b is undefined at a non-word boundary
findings.fix: character-boundary lookarounds (?<![\w])/(?![\w]) allow a leading sign while still blocking '2' matching inside '12'.

findings.issue: runRagPrimaryAgent returns through the CONTROL_MODES branch before findArithmeticSubtasks, so a control-classified arithmetic turn bypassed computed facts and missing_computed_result validation.
findings.reproduction: 'So you can't do math? What is 2+2?' classified CONVERSATIONAL took the control path with no computed fact.
findings.rootCause: arithmetic detection ordered after the early control return
findings.fix: arithmetic-bearing turns (findArithmeticSubtasks on the raw question AND asksForComputedResult) are excluded from the control shortcut and forced through the substantive validated path; the model still writes the prose.
tests: live targeted battery case 12 (control 2+2 gets verified 4)

findings.issue: Normalized non-project entity link list emitted only raw.platform; deployedAt/deployment lost from evidence.
findings.reproduction: product with deployment:'Shopify' produced a chunk without 'Shopify'; a codePen carrying only deployment metadata was skipped entirely.
findings.rootCause: same platform-only hardcoding as finding 4, plus a codePen skip guard that ignored deployment fields
findings.fix: link list includes platform/deployedAt/deployment; codePen skip guard no longer drops entities whose only content is deployment metadata.

findings.issue: CodePen branch recorded codePens[i].platform as source even when the value came from deployedAt/deployment.
findings.reproduction: codePen with deployment:'CodePen.io' → source 'codePens[0].platform'.
findings.rootCause: same hardcoded provenance as finding 5
findings.fix: cpDeployField via find() names the actual source field.

findings.issue: Subject-level goals/availability/preferences were indexed only when objects; canonical schema stores availability as a string, so explicit declarations never became has_property evidence.
findings.reproduction: availability:'Available for remote work' produced no has_property triple.
findings.rootCause: section loop skipped non-object values
findings.fix: string and array-of-strings sections index each entry as a separate property unit with preserved source path and meta.value.

findings.issue: When frame-word filtering emptied propWords, the branch marked the claim supported with no evidence: 'Avery is open to the role' passed on an empty KB.
findings.reproduction: validateRelationships('Avery is open to the role.', emptyKbGraph) returned valid.
findings.rootCause: absence of verifiable content treated as support
findings.fix: empty-content properties are unsupported unless a coherent authored property explicitly proves the claim.

findings.issue: meta.property === objNorm accepted a claim on key existence alone: goals:{relocation:'Not open to relocation'} supported 'Avery is open to relocation'.
findings.reproduction: positive claim validated true against a negated authored value.
findings.rootCause: key match bypassed authored value and polarity
findings.fix: has_property validation now requires the authored value (meta.value / object text) to affirm the predicate; negated values reject; derivational matching in coherentUnitSupports now also checks the negation word list.

findings.issue: m3/m4 future-capability targets captured through end of question: 'Could he become a data engineer requiring Python?' yielded target containing 'requiring Python'.
findings.reproduction: extractRequestedRole returned 'data engineer requiring python'.
findings.rootCause: cleanTarget removed only trailing role nouns/manner words, not requirement suffixes
findings.fix: requirement-boundary vocabulary (requiring/requires/needing/needs/must have/with experience in/with knowledge of/looking for/etc.) now terminates the captured target in cleanRole and cleanTarget.

findings.issue: Hiring/recruiting branch only treated at/with/requiring/requires as boundaries and returned the capture without stripping a requirement suffix: 'hiring for a frontend role needing React' stored 'frontend role needing react' as requestedRole.
findings.reproduction: extractRequestedRole returned 'frontend role needing react'.
findings.rootCause: incomplete boundary marker set; suffix not stripped on this shape
findings.fix: boundary list expanded to the shared requirement vocabulary; 'role needing X' → 'frontend' (the 'role' noun is also dropped since it is syntax, not title).

findings.issue: 'service' in both has_skill and uses_tech facet noun lists made 'What services does Morgan offer?' enumerate JavaScript/React as offered services.
findings.reproduction: facet values included technologies before the fix.
findings.rootCause: facet noun ambiguity resolved without regard to the request predicate
findings.fix: offering verbs (offer/provide/sell) route 'services' to the services collection; tech relations no longer selected for offering predicates.

findings.issue: Attribute fallback searched only products and projects, missing services/CodePens/other normalized collections (e.g. a service's duration).
findings.reproduction: 'What duration does Atlas Consulting have?' returned unsupported.
findings.rootCause: hardcoded collection list
findings.fix: fallback resolves the named entity via normalizeKnowledgeEntities across all collections and reads top-level fields plus attributes/properties.

findings.issue: Named-entity attribute queries returned early when the attribute wasn't a top-level collection, never reaching the entity-attribute fallback ('What price does Northstar Desk have?').
findings.reproduction: facet returned matched:false.
findings.rootCause: early return before entity-attribute resolution when entitySubject present
findings.fix: entity-attribute path stays open when entitySubject resolves; name-part matching repaired so 'Morgan Vale' does not split into subject 'Morgan' + verb 'Vale'.

findings.issue: 'publishin' typo (missing g) meant a captured 'publishing' verb could not select the publications facet.
findings.reproduction: 'What is Morgan publishing?' did not match the publications facet.
findings.rootCause: typo in verb group
findings.fix: corrected to 'publishing'; shape C also accepts is/are/was/were so 'What is X publishing' resolves.

findings.issue: Fallback accepted a technology merely for being in the global knownTechnologies set even when absent from scoped evidence — cross-project overclaim.
findings.reproduction: Project Alpha uses Rust accepted when only Project Beta used Rust.
findings.rootCause: global set used as evidence
findings.fix: removed the global-override return; global set remains usable for alias recognition only.

findings.issue: Early phrase match accepted a technology appearing in negated/unverified evidence ('Rust is not documented' supported 'uses Rust').
findings.reproduction: isTechInEvidence('Rust', 'Rust is not documented.', ['Rust']) returned true.
findings.rootCause: phrase presence checked before polarity/coherence
findings.fix: evidence is split into clauses and checked for affirmative, non-negated mentions; 'does not know COBOL, but has experience with JavaScript' no longer supports COBOL.

summary.duplicateRootCause: findings 14, 15, 20, 23 share root causes with 4, 5, 19, 22 respectively and are covered by the same fixes
